advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) and high coupling (DCC=2) due to direct dependencies on infrastructure classes (OrderRepository, EmailClient), which violates the presentation layer's architectural constraints. Additionally, the `describe_customer` method displays feature envy towards the `Customer` object, accessing its attributes directly rather than delegating to a domain or application service.

suggestions.title: Introduce Application Service for Report Logic
suggestions.sketch: Create a `ReportService` in the application layer that accepts `OrderRepository` and `EmailClient`. Move `order_count` and `mail_summary` logic into this service. `ReportView` should depend on `ReportService` instead of infrastructure classes. This resolves the LV-SKIP violations and reduces DCC by replacing two infrastructure dependencies with one application dependency.

suggestions.title: Delegate Customer Description to Domain
suggestions.sketch: Move the formatting logic from `describe_customer` to a method on the `Customer` domain object (e.g., `Customer.to_display_string(width)`). `ReportView.describe_customer` becomes a simple delegation call. This addresses feature envy and reduces the complexity of the view method.

advices.risk_notes: Moving logic to the application layer requires ensuring the `ReportService` is properly injected into the presentation layer. The domain change for `Customer` may impact other parts of the system if `Customer` is widely used, but adding a display method is generally low-risk. The LCOM4 improvement is moderate because the class will still have distinct responsibilities (title, customer display, report data), but the coupling reduction is significant.
